strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout with a bulk discount (10% off at 10+ items), the SAVE5 coupon (applied after the bulk discount, goods floored at $0, other codes refused) and shipping ($4.99 below $50 of discounted goods, free from $50, nothing for an empty cart). Unit tests on cartTotal in src/cart.js prove each rule and its boundaries. bulkDiscount uses `itemCount > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount, contrary to AC1; TC1 is expected to fail and is reported as a defect. Revision 2 adds TC11 (review finding R1.1): shipping is charged when the subtotal is $50+ but the discounted goods are under $50.
inScope: cartTotal in src/cart.js: bulk discount threshold, SAVE5 coupon order and floor, unknown coupon refusal, shipping threshold on discounted goods, empty cart
outOfScope: Any UI or API for checkout (none exists in the repository)
assumptions: Coupon codes are case-sensitive: the code only knows 'SAVE5', so 'save5' is 'any other coupon code' and is refused.
A non-empty cart whose goods fall to $0 after the coupon still pays $4.99 shipping (AC3 only exempts an empty cart and goods of $50 or more), as the code does.
Money is compared in dollars as numbers rounded to cents, as cartTotal returns them.

risks.description: Off-by-one at the bulk threshold: the code discounts only above 10 items, not at 10.
risks.mitigation: TC1 tests exactly 10 items spread across lines; TC2 and TC3 pin 9 and 11.

risks.description: Coupon applied before the bulk discount gives a different total.
risks.mitigation: TC4 uses amounts where the two orders give different totals.

risks.description: Shipping threshold computed on the pre-discount subtotal or with > instead of >=.
risks.mitigation: TC11 has a $50+ subtotal with goods under $50 after the coupon; TC8/TC9 test $50.00 and $49.99.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets no bulk discount.
Coupon SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, the goods never cost less than $0, and any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when the goods cost $50 or more after discounts, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs $0.

testCases.title: gives 10% off a cart of exactly 10 items spread across lines
steps: Price a cart of $10 x 4 and $10 x 6 with cartTotal
testCases.expected: Total is 90 (100 less 10%, free shipping). Expected to fail against current code (> instead of >=): marked expected-to-fail and reported as a defect.
testCases.rationale: Boundary of the bulk threshold, counting quantities across lines.

defects.title: Bulk discount not applied to a cart of exactly 10 items
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items gets 10% off. src/cart.js bulkDiscount checks `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD` (BULK_THRESHOLD = 10), so exactly 10 items gets no discount. The constant's own doc comment says "at least this many". Expected cartTotal($10x4 + $10x6) = 90; actual 100.
defects.evidence: TC1 asserts cartTotal([{price:10,quantity:4},{price:10,quantity:6}]) === 90; it fails (value 100) and is marked it.fails. TC3 (11 items -> 99) passes.

review.standard: Unit: one reason to fail / a test's name tells you what broke; Test case design: list a criterion on a case only when its assertions would fail if the criterion weren't met
review.summary: TC8 'ships free when the goods cost exactly $50 after discounts' can't tell discounted goods from the pre-discount subtotal: a $55 cart is at least $50 either way, so the test passes if shipping is computed on the subtotal.
review.failureScenario: Suppose cartTotal (src/cart.js:32) is changed to `subtotal(items) >= FREE_SHIPPING_FROM`. The cart [{price:55,quantity:1}] with SAVE5 has a subtotal of 55, so shipping is still free and the total is still 50. TC8 passes, even though the strategy says it proves 'the threshold uses discounted goods'. TC9 ($49.99, no discount) can't catch this either. The only test that fails is TC4 (subtotal 60, goods 49, the result would be 49 instead of 53.99), and it is titled 'takes SAVE5 off after the bulk discount', so the failure would be reported as a coupon-order bug. An exact-$50 case can't separate the two rules, because discounts only lower the price. A separate case is needed where the subtotal is $50 or more and the discounted goods are under $50, for example [{price:52,quantity:1}] with SAVE5, which should give 51.99 (it would give 47 if shipping used the subtotal). TC8 keeps the inclusive >= check, and its title or AC mapping should stop claiming that it checks shipping is based on the discounted goods.
